verses.1: Now, behold, Jehovah is riding on a light horse. He comes from Egypt. The gods of Egypt flee from him. In the hearts of the people of Egypt, there is fear of him.
verses.2: And I will fight against the Egyptians in Egypt. One man will fight against his brother, and one man against his neighbor. One city will fight against another city. One king will fight against another king.
verses.3: And the spirit of Egypt was struck down within him. But his advice was rejected. They went to seek help from the gods, from the magicians, from the shamans, and from the wise men.
verses.4: And I have besieged Egypt with hard rulers. But the king of Egypt will be defeated by God’s power, declares the Lord Almighty.
verses.5: And waters will separate the sea from the land, and rivers will be destroyed and flow away.
verses.6: And the rivers became empty; the gates of the palace were destroyed. The mountains were also ruined.
verses.7: All seeds will be destroyed by the light; all crops will be destroyed by the light. They will be swept away, and they will not remain.
verses.8: And we are the wanderers and those who suffer all kinds of hardships. We wait patiently under the sunlight, and we stand on the shores of the sea, in despair.
verses.9: And the servants of Pishtim cried out in pain and suffered greatly.
verses.10: And her eyes shall be filled with tears, just like all those who work in the pools of tears.
verses.11: But the wise men and advisors of Pharaoh gave him a foolish advice. How could they possibly speak to Pharaoh, son of wisdom? I am a son of kings.
verses.12: May your wisdom be revealed, and may they tell you what Jehovah’s armies have commanded against Egypt.
verses.13: The servants of Zohar carried the servants of Nof. They destroyed Egypt’s rulers.
verses.14: Yehovah sent a swarm of flies into their midst. He destroyed their cities in every way possible, just as a scorpion stings its prey.
verses.15: And there shall be no deed done by the Egyptians that would involve cutting off their heads and tails, as well as destroying their cities.
verses.16: On that day, Egypt will be like women and girls, filled with fear and terror at the sight of the hand of Jehovah’s army that He will raise against it.
verses.17: And the land of Judah would become a source of terror for the Egyptians. Everyone who remembered it would be afraid before the power of Jehovah’s army.
verses.18: On that day, there will be five cities in the land of Egypt. These cities will speak the language of Canaan. They will be devoted to Jehovah, the God of hosts. One of these cities will be destroyed.
verses.19: On that day, it will be sacrificed to Jehovah in the land of Egypt. It will be placed at the border of Egypt, as a sacrifice to Jehovah.
verses.20: And there will be armies of angels for Jehovah in the land of Egypt. They will cry out to Jehovah for help, and He will send them a savior who will save them from their troubles.
verses.21: And Jehovah will know about Egypt, and the people of Egypt will also know about Jehovah on that day. They will offer sacrifices and offerings to Jehovah, and they will worship Him with all their hearts.
verses.22: And Jehovah will smite Egypt with great destruction. They will be destroyed and return to Jehovah. Then He will heal them.
verses.23: On that day, there will be a rebellion from Egypt against Assyria. Assyria and Egypt will also rebel against each other. The people of Egypt will serve Assyria instead of Egypt itself.
verses.24: On that day, Israel will become the third kingdom after Egypt and Assyria, in peace and blessing under the rule of God.
verses.25: May the Lord bless His armies, saying, “Blessed be My people from Egypt, and the work of My hands, Assyria! And my inheritance shall be Israel.”
